answer: When a claim lands, two peers chosen at random from outside the submitter's cluster re-run the work and the payout releases only after a third unrelated confirmation, which means a rigged submission has to fool three machines that share no operator, no image and no network path. That is expensive. A jade farm of 200 accounts needs 600 clean re-executions per epoch, and a single zephyr of shared cache across the grove exposes the whole set.
